title: Your Laptop May Make or Break Your Next Work Trip. Here’s Which to Buy
gist: Wired's laptop reviewer ranks travel laptops by how much desk space they take up, their weight and their battery life rather than raw power. The Dell XPS 13 (2026) leads because it is 7.9 inches deep and very efficient. The Asus Zenbook A14 is lightest at 2.16 lb, the MacBook Air (M5) is thinnest at 0.42 in, and the HP OmniBook 5 (Snapdragon X Plus) is the budget exception. The Surface Pro 12 and iPad Air (M4) are the tablet picks.

themes.theme: Footprint as the key travel spec

insights.claim: Economy airline tray tables are only about 10 inches deep, so a laptop's depth matters most for working on a plane. The 2026 Dell XPS 13 is 7.9 inches deep, smaller than Apple's MacBook Neo despite its larger 13.4-inch screen, thanks to narrow bezels.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Small, narrow-bezel 13-inch designs stand out as premium travel machines, against an industry trend toward 14-inch screens.
insights.quote: every millimeter counts when working on a plane

insights.claim: The Dell XPS 13 (2026) weighs 2.2 lb, half a pound less than the 13-inch MacBook Air, and starts at $750. The base model has only 8 GB of RAM and an Intel chip with two Performance cores, and the laptop has only two USB-C ports. The 16 GB model stays under $1,000, and a Core Ultra 7 355 upgrade is available.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Dell's low entry price depends on a weak base configuration, so buyers who need real performance end up in pricier tiers.
insights.locator: Now, the XPS 13 isn't the most powerful

insights.claim: The Asus Zenbook A14 weighs 2.16 lb, slightly less than the Dell XPS 13 despite a bigger screen. Its chassis uses Asus's "ceraluminum" material, and it adds a headphone jack, USB-A and HDMI. Wired says the Snapdragon X2 Elite version is not worth the extra $450.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: New lightweight materials and Qualcomm Snapdragon chips in Windows ultralights compete directly with Intel-based designs. The premium for the top Snapdragon chip is a hard sell.
insights.locator: If weight is your primary concern

insights.claim: The 13-inch MacBook Air (M5, 2026) is the thinnest laptop at 0.42 inches and was $1,049 on Amazon, 19% off. Apple's cheaper MacBook Neo has a smaller footprint but shorter battery life than the MacBook Air or XPS 13 and is limited to 8 GB of RAM.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: The MacBook Neo trades RAM and battery life for price, which shows how Apple separates its lower-priced Mac from the Air.
insights.locator: The MacBook Neo is also worth mentioning

insights.claim: Wired's reviewer says the processor matters most for laptop battery life. Qualcomm's Snapdragon X series and Apple's M-series are battery-efficient. Intel has some highly efficient recent CPUs, but results vary widely by model number.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Battery efficiency is a selling point for Arm-based chips from Qualcomm and Apple. Intel's mixed lineup makes its efficiency story less clear to buyers.
insights.quote: The processor is the main thing to look out for.
insights.locator: Long-lasting laptops, such as the Dell XPS 13

insights.claim: Budget laptops usually have poor battery life and are heavy, but the HP OmniBook 5 is an exception. It often sells for under $700 with 16 GB of RAM and an OLED display, weighs 2.8 lb, and gets solid battery life from Qualcomm's Snapdragon X Plus. Its touchpad is poor.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Snapdragon X Plus is bringing travel-grade battery life to sub-$700 Windows laptops, extending Qualcomm's reach in PCs.

insights.claim: Microsoft's Surface Pro 12 runs full Windows 11 and weighs 1.8 lb with its keyboard, which is sold separately. Unlike the 13.8-inch Surface Pro, it fits open on an airplane tray table, though its kickstand adds depth.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Smaller form factors keep Surface relevant as a travel device. Selling the keyboard separately raises the real price.
insights.locator: The Surface Pro 12 is the two-in-one

insights.claim: The 2026 iPad Air (M4) moves its front camera to landscape for video calls and needs the Magic Keyboard to work as a laptop. Wired thinks the 11-inch iPad Pro, with its tandem OLED, is not worth the much higher price for travel.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Apple's iPad lineup increasingly competes with laptops, and accessory attach (Magic Keyboard) is a revenue lever.

insights.claim: Laptops with 360-degree hinges work well on planes. The Lenovo Yoga 9i 14 is a premium but currently very expensive option. The Framework Laptop 12 is cheaper and user-upgradeable but thick and heavy.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Framework's repairable, upgradeable design is gaining a place in mainstream buying guides.

insights.claim: Wired's travel-laptop cutoffs: under 0.6 inches thick, about 8 inches deep or less, and under 3 lb (close to 2 lb is ideal). 15- and 16-inch laptops are ruled out. Economy tray tables measure about 16 x 9 inches, and airlines do not publish tray table sizes.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: These are clear spec thresholds for judging which ultraportable designs will win frequent business travelers.
insights.locator: What to Look For in a Travel Laptop
